item.p: Read your packet with tools/spec/spec brief N.M: its text, one line on each decision and packet it cites, and the terms it uses. Open what you need with tools/spec/spec show NAME --depth=2. The rules for parallel packets are in its phase's document (, tools/spec/spec show tasks/phase-N).

Own only the files the packet lists, plus the articles you write. If you need a file another packet owns and has not committed, wait for its commit (git status, git log); never edit it. Put the need to the owner with tools/spec/spec add proposal if it blocks you.

Implementation packets do not change public headers (include/sxml/). If one must change, write the reason as a proposal (tools/spec/spec add proposal) and stop that part. Design packets may change the headers they own. The substrate headers (status, view, memory, string, name, types, tree, xdm, export) are frozen (): additive changes only, each with a decision record.
Name the golden file you imitate in your commit message, and cite the specification sections in comments.

Build in private: never build in the shared build/ directories, because other agents' unfinished files would break the globbed build. Use tools/private-build.sh <scratchpad>/build-<packet> --preset debug -- <your changed or new files>. It builds HEAD plus your files in a snapshot, incrementally on later runs.
Verify in proportion (). The owner runs the full checks on a machine of their own, so a packet does not re-run everything:
the debug preset (Clang with ASan and UBSan) builds with -Werror, and the unit and CLI tests your change touches pass;
clang-tidy is clean on your files, and tools/check-call-cycles.py finds no cycle when you add or change calls between functions;

the conformance test sets your change affects are run with the release driver (sxml-qt4 run, sxml-xslt-test run, sxml-xsd-test run on those sets) and give no fewer passes than before; give before/after counts in the commit message and the LOG entry;
debug-gcc and wasm are built only when the change is platform-sensitive or may grow sxml.wasm noticeably;

full suite runs, all presets, the full lint and fuzzing are left to the owner's machine, unless the packet is a gate review that says otherwise. Never regenerate docs/CONFORMANCE.md from a partial run.
Mark the packet done (tools/spec/spec set-status N.M done), commit and push.

Keep at most one debug and one release snapshot at a time (a debug snapshot is a few GB, a release one about 1.5 GB, almost all of it the test programs); the disk has filled up more than once. Delete your snapshots and scratch directories, then send the final report.
